A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe GRMP-IQA, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. However, v1 refers to AGIQA-3K results in supplementary material and implementation details in an Appendix that are absent from the supplied PDF. Neither supplied file includes an appendix, limiting comparison of those referenced materials.

before.justification: V1 reports original few-shot and supervised IQA experiments, cross-dataset evaluations, component ablations and gMAD examples.

after.justification: V2 retains original IQA experiments and ablations and adds a computational comparison with Q-Align.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 substantively changes the reported meta-prompt optimization. V1 Eq. 6 averages differences between initial and task-updated parameters; v2 instead sums query-loss gradients with respect to the initial parameters after support adaptation. Eq. 5 also changes where the query gradient is evaluated. This revises a central pre-training procedure, although the architecture and QGR remain; the PDFs do not establish implementation changes or reruns.

E1.justification: The seven conventional BIQA datasets and TID2013/KADID-10K pre-training are retained. V1 additionally asserts AGIQA-3K evaluation but places its results in unavailable supplementary material; v2 omits that assertion. Actual removal of AI-generated-image evaluation cannot therefore be reliably established. The retained gMAD examples also do not establish a domain change despite v2 omitting the Waterloo dataset name.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds LoDa to the reduced-data comparison and CDINet to the full-data comparison. New Table 8 compares against Q-Align. Table 1's CLIP and CLIP-IQA rows are relabeled CLIP with Linear Probe and CoOp, respectively, with unchanged scores; these are not additional comparators.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes the reported reduced-data KonIQ training ratio from 30% to 20%. New Table 8 introduces latency and throughput evaluation on an RTX3090 alongside 20%/80% training comparisons. The principal train/test split, few-shot sample counts, backbone and training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 revises the QGR training-dynamics evidence in Figure 4(a) and adds the computational analysis in Table 8. The component, meta-learning and regularization-weight ablations and gMAD examples are retained. V1 Tables 4 and 5 correspond to v2 Tables 5 and 4, rather than new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify median performance across ten splits and retain Figure 2's initialization means, standard deviations and boxplots. V2 moves the ten-split statement into the general implementation section; no increased run count, new uncertainty estimator or statistical test is reported.

E6.justification: Most existing benchmark and tabulated ablation scores are unchanged. Under the revised 30%-to-20% KonIQ setting, GRMP-IQA's PLCC/SRCC changes from 0.936/0.925 to 0.931/0.915, and DEIQT's from 0.922/0.903 to 0.908/0.888; these are replaced results under different conditions. V2 also adds comparator results and changes Figure 4(a)'s trajectory. Table 8 reports throughput of 43.0 versus 9.9 images/second for GRMP-IQA and Q-Align.

T1.justification: Equations 5–6 receive a localized but non-equivalent mathematical revision: the query derivative is evaluated at adapted parameters, and parameter-difference averaging becomes a query-gradient sum. The other defining equations, including the QGR projection, remain unchanged. Neither version adds formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement narrow the reduced-data claim from outperforming or surpassing supervised competitors to being competitive with them. V2 foregrounds Few-Shot IQA and removes the introductory claim about competitive KonIQ performance with 2% training data. The two central technical contributions remain meta-prompt pre-training and QGR.

C2.justification: V2 adds an interpretation of CoOp's limited advantage over linear probing through the mismatch between semantic pre-training and distortion sensitivity. It qualifies cross-dataset superiority from all six experiments to most scenarios and describes the revised no-QGR trajectory as saturation with slight decline rather than a sharp drop. The gradient-angle discussion also becomes more cautious, emphasizing variation and suggesting correlations.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, four-RTX3090 hardware disclosure, 41M trainable/151M total parameter counts, and reproduction markers for selected Table 1 results. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit statement that the gMAD models were trained on LIVE and tested on Waterloo. Most existing hyperparameters remain documented unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references and discussion concerning meta-regularized prompting, semantic/distortion disentanglement, Q-Align and CDINet. It explicitly distinguishes its distortion-based meta-tasks from semantic-category meta-prompt methods. Some earlier coverage, including Kg-CoOp and NLP prompt-transfer references, is removed, while the overall BIQA and prompt-tuning positioning remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method explanations and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Separate few-shot and supervised comparison sections are merged into Section 4.3, and qualitative analysis becomes Section 4.6 instead of a standalone section. The title, author block and contribution wording also change.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 8, expands Table 2, redraws Figure 4(a), and updates Figure 3's annotations and connections, including its equation reference. Existing tables and plots are rearranged, captions and highlighting are restyled, and Tables 4–5 exchange numbering. Most underlying visual material, including Figures 1–2 and the gMAD images, is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies motivation and research positioning, moderates several performance claims, adds useful comparator and efficiency evidence, and supplies code and hardware disclosures. These improve a paper whose principal experimental evidence is largely retained. The gains are limited by lost gMAD setup details and an overbroad claim of accuracy superiority over Q-Align: Table 8 reports lower full-data SRCC for GRMP-IQA, 0.934 versus 0.940, despite higher PLCC.
